subject: Post-call recap + fallback playbook (reliability focus) — SentryGuard
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Romero <alex@sentryguard.io>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, dev.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 21 Mar 2026 16:04:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + initial next steps — reliability & graceful degradation

Alex — thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our 45-minute discovery so we have alignment before the POC kickoff: 

Summary of pain points you shared
- Recent spike in latency and two partial outages in Feb/Mar during batch processing windows (attached timeline).
- Primary customer impact: delayed alert delivery and increased false positives when the scoring pipeline falls back to synchronous scoring.
- Current ops burden: manual failover to warm standby and runbook steps that take ~12–18 minutes.

Current stack (what you told us)
- Inference: hosted endpoints from a managed vendor + internal k8s workers for heavy throughput paths.
- Orchestration: internal API gateway in us-west-2; replica region us-east-1 used ad-hoc; no active-active routing today.
- Models: two-tier stack — large base model (1.3B/13B variants) for high-fidelity scoring + a distilled 350M model used only during incidents.

Success criteria for the initial POC
- Maintain customer-facing scoring SLA: p95 latency < 200ms for inference requests under steady state.
- Graceful degradation: automatic fallback to smaller model within 5s of degraded health without user-visible errors.
- Recovery/runbooks: <2 minute automated cutover to fallback path; manual intervention only for escalations.

Suggested next steps (what we agreed on)
1) Provide the incident timeline and sample traces (attached: sentryguard-incident-timeline.xlsx).
2) Redwood to propose a fallback playbook with model/region routing, KV cache warmup, and canarying steps (deliverable: proposed-fallback-matrix.pdf).
3) Technical kickoff next Tuesday 3/24 — 60 min with our infra eng + your SREs to finalize the MAP.
4) POC scope: 2-week dedicated capacity trial + runbook automation (we outlined options below).

Open questions for your team
- Are there compliance or network constraints for cross-region traffic we should account for?
- Any hard cutover windows (daily batch jobs) where we must avoid rollout steps?

Attachments: sentryguard-incident-timeline.xlsx (spreadsheet with timestamps), proposed-fallback-matrix.pdf (draft).

Thanks — marking the calendar invite after I sync internally.

— Markus Klein
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0142

Markus — appreciate the thorough recap. Confirming a few details and adding context from our side:

Incident details
- Two incidents: 2026-02-11 (partial region outage — 18m) and 2026-03-05 (degraded tail latency — ~1.5 hours). Both caused customer-facing delays and elevated support tickets.
- Root cause hypothesis: synchronous scoring queue exhaustion under batch spike + aggressive autoscaler cooldowns.

What we need from Redwood in the POC
- A concrete fallback matrix that specifies: model hierarchy, per-model latency expectations, cache warm-start behavior, and how traffic will be diverted across regions.
- A proposed SLO baseline we can commit to for the trial (we prefer to see 99.9% availability and p95 < 200ms but want tradeoffs documented).

Network/compliance notes
- No external cross-border restrictions; us-west-2 primary, us-east-1 secondary is acceptable. We do need a diagram for our security review though (VPC peering / private link).

I'll get our SRE leads to review the timeline attachment and drop any redlines tomorrow. If we can get the fallback playbook before Mon EOD that would help speed up the kickoff.

Thanks — Alex

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: markus.klein@redwood.ai, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call recap + initial next steps — reliability & graceful degradation

Markus / Lauren — draft plan below; aiming to get a one-page playbook to deliver by Mon morning. High-level technical approach: 

1) Health detection
- Signals: p95 latency > 200ms sustained for 30s OR 5xx rate > 1% over 1m triggers degraded state.
- Primary monitor lives in us-west-2; replicated metrics to us-east-1 for failover awareness.

2) Fallback sequence (automated)
- Step A: reduce batch sizes + enable KV cache-only responses for known prefixes (fast path) — should reduce tail latency immediately.
- Step B: route a percentage (20% -> 50% -> 100%) of traffic to distilled 350M model while maintaining a canary to the larger model for quality checks.
- Step C: if region-level health remains degraded, shift region routing to us-east-1 with prefetched KV cache and warmed weights on dedicated nodes.

3) Timings and expectations
- Detection -> Step A within 15–30s, Step B engaged within 60s, full fallback within 120–300s depending on cache warmup speed. We can tune toward their 5s ask by prewarming critical keys for high-risk customers as part of the POC.
- Expected perf: p95 on 350M model ~70–120ms (depending on request size); larger models p95 140–220ms under normal ops.

4) Infrastructure recommendation for POC
- Use Redwood Dedicated for predictable capacity and strict isolation for their sensitive workloads.
- Provision small multi-region pool (us-west-2 primary, us-east-1 standby) with reserved warm nodes and a takeover script; include a fallback router in the control plane with canary sampling.

5) Deliverables for Mon
- One-page fallback playbook (PDF)
- Detailed matrix with thresholds and expected latencies (spreadsheet)
- Draft runbook snippets for SREs (cutover + rollback)

I'll attach the draft matrix and runbook snippets to the playbook. If we want to hit 5s cutover for select customers we should identify a list of top 10 high-priority shopper IDs to prewarm — SentryGuard to provide.

— Dev Patel
Staff Site Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
